subject: Hard routing exception: EU-only model enforcement + no-fallback — cloudmed request
messages:
From: Asha Verma <asha.verma@cloudmed.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Oct 2026 08:12:00 +0000
Subject: Request: EU-only routing + no-fallback requirement for CloudMed PII flows

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the call this week. CloudMed has completed an internal data residency review and our privacy team is requiring that all inference requests for the new PII redaction pipeline be pinned to EU-only execution — specifically eu-west-1 — with no cross-region fallback under any circumstance.

Concretely, we need:
- A hard region lock to eu-west-1 for model execution.
- No automatic fallback to other regions (including US) even during capacity or outage events.
- Forced selection of your eu-quantized-3b model variant (we'll provide the model id) for this route.

We understand this is a heavy constraint; CloudMed is willing to contract for reserved Dedicated capacity if needed. We also need an audit trail showing routing enforcement and a short playbook for incident handling (who to call, what steps to take) since our security team will require that in the contract.

I've attached our Routing_SLA_Request.pdf with the security checklist. Can you confirm feasibility and a rough timeline? Our procurement window is end of month.

Best,
Asha
Procurement & Security Lead
CloudMed

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: EU-only routing + no-fallback requirement for CloudMed PII flows

Thanks — high-level feasibility notes below. TL;DR: technically possible but with operational risk; recommend dedicated capacity + explicit SLA and an incident runbook.

Technical constraints and proposal:
- Region lock: we already support region affinity routing. We can implement a strict policy to only route to eu-west-1 for this customer route. That part is straightforward.
- No-fallback enforcement: currently our routing engine supports prioritized fallback chains (preferred -> secondary -> failover). Turning off fallback (i.e., fail-closed) is implementable, but it means that during any eu-west-1 capacity shortage or instance-level outage the request will fail immediately.
- Forced model selection: we can pin to eu-quantized-3b for the route. We'll need the exact model identifier and to ensure it's loaded and kept warm on reserved nodes.

Operational impacts:
- Latency/cost: to guarantee availability with no fallback, customer must reserve headroom (Dedicated capacity) or accept request failures. If they choose dedicated, we should size buffer for typical peaks + 25% buffer.
- Observability/audit: we can provide routing audit logs (trace IDs, model id, node id) and integrate with their SIEM via webhook.
- Incident playbook: provisioning a distinct on-call rotation for that Dedicated pool is recommended.

Steps I propose:
1) Create JIRA-ROUTE-2981 for an EU-hardlock configuration flag (owner: infra-routing).
2) Provision a small Dedicated pool for CloudMed in eu-west-1 for validation (proof-of-concept).
3) In parallel, draft a signed addendum that states "no-fallback = fail-closed" and includes agreed SLAs and credit calculations for downtime. Legal/commercial to finalize.

If CloudMed insists on no-fallback and refuses dedicated capacity, we should refuse to accept the clause (too high risk).

I'll attach an ops impact matrix to quantify resource needs.

Marcus
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

Attachment: ops-impact-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 09:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: EU-only routing + no-fallback requirement for CloudMed PII flows

Couple of product/roadmap notes from my side:

- Feature vs config: The short-term path Marcus outlined (a config flag to set "fail-closed" for a route) is acceptable as a feature toggle. We need to scope work to ensure it's limited to routing metadata and doesn't change global routing behaviors. Time estimate: ~3 sprints to implement + 1 sprint for QA and canary.
- Priority: we can slot it as a P2 if CloudMed is signing a Dedicated contract; otherwise it's P3. We should get commercial confirmation before we start dev work.
- Compatibility: ensure the flag is supported by both Hosted and Dedicated: Hosted would enforce the lock at the control plane, Dedicated would be enforced locally on the customer's pool.
- Edge case: model variant load failure (e.g., quantized artifact corrupt). If the model fails to load, our current behavior is to attempt fallback to the latest compatible variant. For this customer, fallback is forbidden, so we must add a policy that surfaces a clear error and triggers immediate ops paging. This requires small changes in the model loader error handling.

I'll open a roadmap ticket and link JIRA-ROUTE-2981. If @Marissa confirms commercial/contract approach, we can start a small spike next week.

-karthik
Product Manager, Routing

Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: EU-only routing + no-fallback requirement for CloudMed PII flows

Thanks everyone — Asha, appreciate the detail in the PDF. Quick summary and next steps so CloudMed has clarity: 

1) Feasibility: Redwood can implement a hard region lock to eu-west-1 and enforce a fail-closed (no-fallback) policy, and we can pin the route to the eu-quantized-3b model variant. Marcus: please ensure we document the model id and load verification steps.
2) Risk & commercial: Marissa, we'll need a written addendum that specifies: reserved capacity sizing, explicit SLA for availability (with credits), and acceptance of failure semantics if eu-west-1 experiences platform-level outages.
3) Implementation plan: Karthik to own the routing flag JIRA-ROUTE-2981 and deliver a spike next week (estimate 3 sprints to GA if approved). Marcus to provision a short-lived Dedicated pool for validation and create the ops runbook/paging playbook.
4) Timeline: target proof-of-concept in eu-west-1 by 2026-10-24 if Dedicated pool is approved; final delivery contingent on contract.

Asha — can you confirm whether CloudMed will proceed with Dedicated capacity commitment? If yes, we'll start the spike and provisioning immediately. If no, we should plan to decline the no-fallback clause and advise a fallback policy with strict routing preferences instead.

I'll schedule a 30-minute alignment call for Tuesday with product, infra, and security to confirm scope. Marcus/Marissa/Karthik please add the documents to the Drive link and update JIRA-ROUTE-2981 with estimates.

Evelyn
Senior Director, Partnerships
Redwood Inference
